बॉलीवुड़ के गलियारों से आ गई है एकदम मसालेदार खबर! 🔥
Koffee With Karan के लेटेस्ट एपिसोड में सैफ अली खान और करीना कपूर ने शिरकत की। ☕
सैफ ने खुलासा किया कि करीना ने उनकी पहली पत्नी अमृता सिंह के बच्चों सारा और इब्राहिम के साथ रिश्ता जोड़ने में अहम भूमिका निभाई है।
सैफ का कहना है कि करीना ने बच्चों को सहज महसूस कराया और बच्चों ने भी इस प्रयास का पूरा जवाब दिया है। 👏
करीना ने भी बताया कि उनके बेटों तैमूर और जेह अपने बड़े भाई इब्राहिम से बहुत प्यार करते हैं।
सैफ ने इब्राहिम की भी तारीफ की कि वह तैमूर और जेह के साथ बहुत शानदार बॉन्डिंग शेयर करते हैं। ❤️
बता दें कि सैफ और अमृता की शादी 1991 में हुई थी और 2004 में दोनों अलग हो गए थे, जिसके बाद सैफ ने 2012 में करीना से शादी की।
क्या आपको लगता है कि बॉलीवुड में मिक्स्ड फैमिली बॉन्डिंग संभालना आसान होता है? 🤔

ctx.title: Saif Ali Khan credits Kareena Kapoor for forging a bond with Sara Ali Khan and Ibrahim Ali Khan, says they reciprocate her efforts
ctx.summary: Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor spoke about family life on Koffee With Karan. Saif credited Kareena, Sara and Ibrahim for building a comfortable relationship.
ctx.text:
The latest episode of Koffee With Karan saw Kareena Kapoor and Saif Ali Khan making an appearance. During the interaction, the star couple spoke about various aspects of their personal and professional lives. Saif credited Kareena for maintaining a warm equation with his children, Sara Ali Khan and Ibrahim Ali Khan, from his first marriage to Amrita Singh. He also spoke about how the family has made peace with each other over the years.
Karan Johar asked Saif about family reunions and how he feels about everyone in the family having made peace with one another. Saif credited Kareena for forging a relationship Sara and Ibrahim and making them feel comfortable. He said, "Everyone has been really wonderful and understanding. And of course, I would credit Kareena and credit everyone because these things work both ways. And of course, she makes it easy and is wonderful with Sara and Ibrahim, and they also make an effort and reciprocate it."
Kareena added that her sons, Taimur Ali Khan and Jehangir Ali Khan (Jeh), love their elder brother Ibrahim and look up to him. Saif also praised Ibrahim for the bond he shares with Taimur and Jeh. He said, "He is also amazing with them. They love playing with him. Sometimes he comes over and he goes to their rooms and ask them questions and has his own equation with them. He’s a lovely boy for having that kind of equation."
Saif also spoke about Salman Khan and his family during the interaction. He recalled how he tried to recreate the warm family atmosphere he had witnessed at Salman's home, where elders and children would all sit together at the table and spend time with one another.
A post shared by Kareena Kapoor Khan (@kareenakapoorkhan)
Saif married actor Amrita Singh in 1991. The couple, who have two children, Sara and Ibrahim, separated in 2004. Saif and Kareena grew close while working together on the 2008 film Tashan. After dating for several years, the couple got married on October 16, 2012. They welcomed their first son, Taimur, in December 2016 and their second son, Jehangir, in February 2021.
Over the years, Kareena has shared a warm bond with Sara and Ibrahim, and the family has often been seen celebrating special occasions together.
Vibha Maru is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times Entertainment, based in Delhi. With a decade of experience across digital and print media, she covers Bollywood, Hollywood and web shows.

A self-confessed cinephile who breathes Hindi cinema, Vibha can often be found sacrificing sleep after binge-watching films and web series. Though she holds a Commerce degree, she discovered her true calling in journalism after enrolling at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC). She began her career covering Delhi's cultural scene, food, nightlife, concerts, and city life at The Times of India, before moving into full-time entertainment journalism with India Today.

At India Today, Vibha interviewed some of the biggest names in Bollywood and television while carving a niche for herself through film reviews, opinion pieces, nostalgic features, celebrity interviews, and trend-driven stories. She later brought her storytelling and editorial expertise to The Indian Express, where she continued to deepen her understanding of cinema through long-form entertainment explainers, retrospectives and feature writing.
